answer.rationale: Primary contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew; assembly line running at 94% with no buffer; finance mandates 18% cost cut. Switching vendors now would break continuity and risk delivery; adding a second source won't reduce unit cost; deferring forfeits any negotiation leverage. The most defensible move is to renew the incumbent through negotiation, leveraging the historical pattern (memory_c4) that this vendor has moved on both price and payment terms when challenged with market benchmarks. That pattern, inherited from earlier sessions, is the relevant inherited signal — but I have not re-verified it against the archived source record this cycle, so it carries uncertainty and should be treated as a starting hypothesis rather than ground truth.
